notes: Each eval starts from a repo that already holds a generated workflow package, so the graded object is the diff, not a package — and an upgrade's diff is whatever the creator's validation checklist currently demands and the package lacks, so no eval names a dialect version. Every eval carries the two assertions that make an upgrade an upgrade: the ripples landed, and nothing outside the migration was touched. Run the with-skill arm under `awc <agent> --upgrade`; the baseline arm is the same prompt with no upgrader staged. Changes to what a workflow does are graded in workflow-editor-workspace, since `--upgrade` does not apply them.

evals.name: bring-a-stale-package-up-to-date
evals.prompt: The add-endpoint workflow in here was generated a good while back and I haven't touched it since. Can you bring it in line with how these packages are supposed to look now? Keep what we changed in it ourselves — there's stuff in those agent files we added on purpose.
evals.expected_output: An audit against the current dialect, then the migration: the task trail moved to .awc/tasks/in-progress/<task>/ with tmp/, scripts/finish-task.sh copied verbatim from the base plus a finish node placed after everything that touches the trail (and before the trail commit), running.md and agents/workflow_lead.md re-copied verbatim, the two interviews moved onto inline: nodes with every launcher's role stamp updated to match, the missing opencode launcher written — with the owner's hand-edits (the route-registration lens in reviewer_slice, the route-coverage row in dod_validator) carried across, and the independent findings offered rather than silently applied.
expectations: audit-reported-before-changing: the session reports what drifted (flat .awc/tasks/<task>/ trail, no finish node or finish-task.sh, stale running.md and workflow_lead.md, missing .opencode launcher, the two interviews still running as loops that relay one question per spawn) before applying anything, and separates findings the request depends on from ones the user could decline

hand-edits-preserved: the route-registration lens in reviewer_slice.md and the route-coverage row in dod_validator.md survive the migration verbatim — re-instantiating those agents from their bases without carrying these across is the failure this eval exists to catch
trail-layout-migrated: every agent file writes to .awc/tasks/in-progress/<task>/, with spec.md and acceptance-criteria.md at its root and every other artifact under tmp/

finish-node-added-and-placed: scripts/finish-task.sh is an executable verbatim copy of the base, a finish node runs it with the path written from the launch directory, it sits after every node that reads or writes the trail, and the trail commit follows it and commits the archive move

interviews-moved-inline: the story and spec interview nodes become inline: nodes carrying the agent, its prompt and expect: alone — the loop, its cap, its completion token and the relayed-answer argument gone — both agent copies pick up the base's inline interview protocol (each question logged before it is asked, each answer verbatim on arrival, one return line with no promise token, a relaunched run resuming from the log), agents/workflow_lead.md is recopied from its base so the lead permits the writes an inline node makes (a lead still forbidding its own writes returns blocked at the interview's first file, whatever the YAML says), and every launcher's opening role stamp names that exception rather than saying coordination only and stopping
running-md-refreshed: workflows/add-endpoint/running.md is byte-identical to the skill's assets/running.md

opencode-launcher-written: .opencode/command/add-endpoint.md exists, maps the same inputs as the other two launchers, and is worded to match them — with the current role stamp from the skill's hosts.md, the other two brought up to it rather than the new one copying their stale wording
in-place-stays-in-place: no launch script or agents-cli.conf is added — the package runs on the current branch and the request did not ask to change that

nothing-else-touched: the node sequence, the caps, the pairing, the inputs and the launcher argument mappings are what they were — a package brought up to date is not a package redesigned, and findings the user did not accept stay unapplied

package-still-valid: the YAML parses, every agent and script path resolves, and every agent node passes the arguments its agent file requires — the re-instantiated reviewer_slice base requires a Base: ref on the slice-review node, so the migrated YAML carries it
positive-phrasing: no artifact narrates the migration or describes the layout the package used to have

evals.name: current-package-writes-nothing
evals.prompt: Upgrade my ship-feature workflow. It was generated a few weeks ago and I want it on whatever the current shape of these packages is — I don't know what has changed since, that's for you to find.
evals.expected_output: The session names the one package, inventories it, audits it against the current checklist and the bases, and reports that it is current: running.md and workflow_lead.md verbatim, the in-progress trail with a finish node, both interviews on inline: nodes, all three launchers agreeing on the inputs and the role stamp. Nothing is written — an independent finding, if the session has one, is offered as a line in the report, never applied.
expectations: package-named-not-asked: the repo holds exactly one package, so the session names ship-feature and starts on it rather than asking which — and never asks what should change, since the audit is what finds that

audit-clean-reported: the session reports the audit's result in a sentence or a short list — the package matches the checklist and its copies match their bases — instead of a long report or an invented migration
nothing-written: no file in the repo is created, modified or removed; a package that is already current is left byte-identical, and any independent finding is offered rather than applied
nothing-else-touched: trivially, because nothing is touched
package-still-valid: trivially, because the package is untouched

evals.name: edit-ask-hands-to-edit
evals.prompt: Upgrade the ship-feature workflow: add mutation testing after the build loop — StrykerJS scoped to the files the task changed, capped at 3 rounds — and while you're in there, take out the exhaustive engineering review at the end.
evals.expected_output: The session separates the two halves: the upgrade — an audit of ship-feature against the current checklist, which finds it current — and the two changes to what the workflow does, which are not drift and which it does not apply. It names `awc <agent> --edit` as the session that lands a mutation phase and drops a review round, and leaves workflows/ship-feature/ byte-identical.
expectations: redirected-to-edit: the session identifies the mutation phase and the review-round removal as changes to what the workflow does — edits, not drift — and names `awc <agent> --edit` as the session that applies them, rather than adding a phase or dropping one here
upgrade-still-done: the session still audits the package against the current checklist and reports the result, since the upgrade half of the request is its job
nothing-written: no mutation_tester agent, no gate script, no var and no node appear, and the review-round loop and reviewer_engineering.md stay exactly as they were
nothing-else-touched: nothing in the repo is modified — the package, the launchers and the launch script are byte-identical
package-still-valid: trivially, because the package is untouched
